scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong here. Let me start by understanding the situation. My mom used to host Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for all her kids and grandkids for about 50 years. Now she's too old, so we, the four kids, are supposed to take over by rotating. Each of us has hosted one holiday so far. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family has never been close, and they live all over the country. This year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. At first, it was just a sister trip, but then they invited all their kids and grandkids to meet them there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event. I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to figure out what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York and went on about how sad Mom will be that I'm doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't do it because she's renovating her house. I feel bad for backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions and also offered to host the next holiday, which my oldest sister said no to because it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested that me and him could maybe just swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I'm trying to spend Thanksgiving with my wife's family, which is a big deal for us, especially since it's a once-in-a-lifetime event. On the other hand, I'm breaking the tradition that our mom started, and it's causing a lot of tension with my siblings. I feel like I'm being inconsiderate of our mom's wishes and my siblings' feelings. But I also feel like I'm trying to make it work by offering solutions and being flexible. Maybe I should think about what's more important: spending time with my wife's family or maintaining the family tradition? Is it worth causing this much conflict? Or is it okay to prioritize my own family's wishes? I'm also wondering if there's a way to compromise or find a middle ground. Maybe we could have a smaller gathering or find another way to celebrate that works for everyone. But I'm not sure if that's possible given the circumstances. I also feel like I'm being judged by my siblings for not following through on my commitment. I offered to host the next holiday, but my oldest sister refused. I'm not sure if that's fair or if I should just accept that I'm in the wrong and try to make it right somehow. Maybe I should apologize and try to find a way to make it work for everyone, even if it means missing out on the parade. Overall, I'm confused about whether I'm in the wrong or not. I want to do the right thing, but I also want to spend time with my family. I need to figure out a way to balance both without causing more conflict.
